title: serve versioned public assets through a configured CDN
input: The site owner publishes immutable assets and configures the currently supported CDN profile and origin.
action: The CDN caches and serves permitted HTTP assets from the configured origin under its cache and delivery rules. The origin application handles uncached requests; private responses require deliberately safe cache settings.
output: The browser downloads public assets while authenticated API requests follow their separate protected endpoint.
check: Verify cache keys, purge behavior, origin restrictions and the selected product's migration lifecycle.

service: Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools
title: extract reviewed fields from a business document
input: The document application submits an authorized invoice with the selected analyzer schema.
action: Content Understanding applies the configured supported analyzer to the input and returns structured fields or content insights. The analyzer definition determines the requested extraction; the application validates fields before financial use.
output: The invoice handler presents uncertain amounts or identifiers to a reviewer before posting to the ledger.
check: Compare totals and source evidence, reject unsupported fields and test privacy boundaries on sample invoices.

title: assist an operator investigating a cloud resource
input: The operator selects the affected resource and a bounded diagnostic question.
action: Azure Copilot assists supported Azure administration tasks using available resource context and the user's permissions. Suggestions require operator validation; a generated explanation is not proof of the resource's actual state.
output: The operator reviews the suggested investigation or change and applies only an approved supported action.
check: Confirm resource identifiers, permissions and post-change behavior against direct service evidence.

title: import an offline archive into Azure storage
input: The archive owner inventories files, orders a supported device and prepares authorized local copy access.
action: Data Box receives the local dataset through the selected device interface and follows the approved return and cloud-import procedure. The destination storage account and encryption controls define the imported dataset boundary.
output: The cloud ingestion team accepts the imported blobs after checking completeness and access permissions.
check: Reconcile checksums and missing files, document custody and retain the source until cloud acceptance.

title: share an approved dataset with a business partner
input: The data owner selects supported datasets and grants the partner an explicit sharing invitation.
action: Data Share coordinates the configured supported sharing or snapshot workflow and recipient acceptance. Source and recipient permissions determine which data is copied or accessed; the owner retains responsibility for permitted content.
output: The partner uses the accepted shared dataset within its agreed analysis scope.
check: Check snapshot freshness, destination permissions and revocation behavior; previously copied data needs separate contractual handling.

title: move a historical managed MariaDB application to a supported target
input: The database owner exports schema, rows, routines and engine-specific application dependencies.
action: The retired managed MariaDB deployment historically executed relational SQL for the application. Migration selects a supported compatible database and transforms unsupported syntax or features explicitly.
output: The target backend uses the validated schema and connection settings after an accepted data transfer.
check: Compare transaction results, collation, routines and final-write reconciliation before switching the application.

title: commit checkout transactions in managed MySQL
input: The checkout backend submits validated order rows through its restricted database account.
action: The selected managed MySQL server executes SQL transactions and stores the relational order data. Engine settings, indexes and availability configuration determine performance and recovery; application code owns order validation.
output: The checkout backend returns the committed order identifier and queries only permitted customer records.
check: Test conflicting writes, connection recovery, backup restore and supported MySQL features with the actual schema.

title: reserve a booking with a managed PostgreSQL transaction
input: The booking backend submits a validated slot and stable request identifier.
action: The managed PostgreSQL server executes the application's SQL transaction and constraints. The schema prevents conflicting reservations; application retry logic resolves uncertain commit results without creating duplicate bookings.
output: The backend returns the committed reservation and reads it under the caller's authorized scope.
check: Test concurrent bookings, failover, connection pooling and point-in-time recovery using the production schema.

title: place licensed application VMs on dedicated physical capacity
input: The platform owner selects supported host capacity, VM sizes and applicable software licensing requirements.
action: Dedicated Host allocates supported physical hosts dedicated to the customer's VM placement. VMs run the application; host-group and placement configuration govern capacity and supported maintenance behavior.
output: The licensed application serves approved enterprise clients from VMs placed on the selected hosts.
check: Check placement, licensing evidence, spare capacity and application recovery during maintenance or host failure.

title: create a reviewed development environment from a catalog
input: The platform team defines an approved environment template and developer deployment parameters.
action: Deployment Environments coordinates supported environment creation from the configured catalog and project settings. The deployment applies the template under the assigned identity; deployed resources run the actual test application.
output: The developer uses the created environment for the feature's integration tests and removes it when finished.
check: Verify allowed templates, deployment permissions, resource cost limits and complete cleanup of temporary environments.
